messages.text: I jumped the gun and flashed it with Rev 5 1. its running 4.9TH
Searched the web · Harlo OS NerdQX firmware rev 5.1 6.1 7

Hi, I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist.

Good news first: 4.9 TH/s is not a sign you broke anything. A quad BM1370 board like the NerdQX runs right around 4.8 TH/s at its stock 600 MHz setting. 
Stock performance is approximately 4.8 TH/s at 69.5W
, and the 8 TH/s figure is the tuned number: 
at the full 1000 MHz the unit hits 8.1 TH/s at 140 watts
. That matches the 145 W at the wall on the product page.

So the unit is behaving. Before anything else, one check:

1. Open the dashboard and tell me the frequency (MHz) and core voltage (mV) it is showing right now.
2. While you are there, tell me the firmware version string exactly as it appears.

That tells me whether the build you flashed is holding you at the 600 MHz stock tier or at a lower ceiling, and whether it matches your actual board.

One warning before you touch the clock: 
the included 124 watt supply crosses its 99.2 watt continuous rating at around 108 watts of draw
, so the higher tiers need a bigger PSU, and 
older board revisions used a three-phase regulator that ran short on thermal margin at high sustained frequencies
. Do not push it until we know which board you have.

JD is still confirming the exact Harlo OS build for the NerdQX. Fastest route if you want it now: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and mention @nullhashrate.

That changes things in your favour. 12V 18A gives you 216 W, so with 80% derating you have roughly 173 W continuous available. The 140 W draw at the top tier sits comfortably inside that, so the power supply is not your limit. The limits left are the board revision (regulator headroom) and the firmware ceiling.

Still need the two numbers from the dashboard before we touch anything:

1. Frequency in MHz and core voltage in mV.
2. The firmware version string, exactly as shown.

And one more, since you flashed a Rev 5.1 build: look at the PCB itself, usually silkscreened near an edge or by the connector, and tell me what revision is printed there. If the board is a newer revision than the build you flashed, you are likely cap····lower frequency ceiling than the hardware can do, and that alone would explain sitting at the stock tier.
